articleTitle: Features of Thermostatic Systems for Vehicles with Hydrogen Fuel Cells
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: The development of hydrogen energy has contributed to the use of hydrogen fuel cells in motor vehicles as an environmentally friendly energy source. The article discusses the operating principle of a hydrogen fuel cell, as well as various methods of removing heat from the cells. The advantages and disadvantages of fuel cell cooling methods are noted. The operating schemes of hydrogen fuel cells, including the thermostatic system, are given. The main differences between the thermostatic system of a car with an internal combustion engine and a car with hydrogen fuel cells are shown. The main models of cars with hydrogen fuel cells are listed.

articleTitle: Distributed and Timely Smart Microgrid Management Through Markov Games
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: Energy delivery within smart microgrids often requires prompt reaction to the system state. In the presence of multiple energy sources, inefficiency may arise due to their lack of coordination. In this paper, we frame the task of efficient energy management as a dynamic program, and we further expand it to the case of multiple agents. We combine this approach with game theory and we leverage the similarity between Markov games concerning information and energy exchanges in networks. This methodological motivation allows us to identify distributed control techniques for efficient energy delivery. Specifically, we highlight how a naive distributed and selfish control of individual nodes may be inefficient from a game theoretic perspective. Yet, a decentralized strategy that combines energy availability and global network cost as shared objectives can significantly improve the outcome, approaching the performance of a centralized resource allocation still in a distributed manner.

articleTitle: Power Reduction and Efficiency Improvement of a Variable-Pitch Axial Flow Fan Obtained from Design Optimization Study
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: The present paper deals with the optimization study of an axial flow fan, which optimizes 3D fan rotor blade geometry by the application of optimization algorithm to the design variables of spanwise camber, stagger angles and chord lengths for improving fan performance and maximizing fan efficiency. Through the design optimization process of fan rotor blade, optimal fan rotor is obtained and then coupled with outlet guide vane. Computational fluid dynamics analysis is conducted to verify the performance and efficiency of the present optimal fan design. The design values of performance and efficiency of the present optimal fan agree well with the CFD results and the present optimal fan design gives the efficiency improvement of 6.7% compared to the initial design.

articleTitle: An Improved Circulating Current Suppression Control Scheme for MMC-based HVDC Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: Recent advancements in Modular Multilevel Converter (MMC) technology have garnered considerable interest, particularly for high-voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission systems, due to its reduced losses in power system. Despite these benefits, a significant challenge in MMC-based HVDC systems is managing circulating current, which can result in increased losses, diminished system efficiency, and compromised stability. This study introduces a control strategy aimed at suppressing circulating current in MMC-based HVDC systems. The strategy utilizes a double fundamental frequency and a negative sequence rotational frame. Through vector current control, alternating quantities are converted into dq quantities and managed with PI controllers. This control approach has been evaluated in a two-terminal MMC-based HVDC system, demonstrating advantages such as reduced circulating current, decreased distortions in submodule voltages and arm currents, and improved total harmonic distortion (THD). The proposed control strategy does not affect the AC dynamics of test system.

articleTitle: Showcasing Battery Energy Storage for Enhanced Grid Stability: A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: This paper presents the results of a case study showcasing a battery energy storage system designed to enhance grid stability. The showcase was carried out over a period of one year in a substation located in the distribution region of ADM Energy Distribution Company, with the aim of demonstrating the effectiveness of battery energy storage for supporting the overall sustainability of power systems. Two battery energy storage systems, with capacities of 250kW/224 kWh each, were configured to provide various grid services, including peak shaving, reactive support, voltage regulation, and microgrid operation. The showcase demonstrated that the battery energy storage system was able to respond rapidly to grid conditions and was effective in smoothing out the variability. The battery energy storage system also provided reliable grid support during peak demand periods, reducing the need for conventional generation resources thus reducing the need of infrastructure investments. The case study provides important insights into the effectiveness of battery energy storage systems for supporting renewable energy integration and enhancing the sustainability of power systems. The results have important implications for the wider adoption of distributed renewable energy and battery energy storage systems in Europe and around the world. Overall, this showcase provides a compelling example of how battery energy storage can play a key role in the transition to a more sustainable and renewable energy future. The findings are of interest to a wide range of stakeholders, including policymakers, energy companies, and researchers, and have the potential to inform future investment decisions in renewable energy and battery energy storage. The showcased BESS exhibited rapid response to grid conditions, effectively mitigating variability and ensuring reliability during peak demand periods. By reducing reliance on conventional generation resources, the BESS contributed to infrastructure optimization, demonstrating potential cost savings. The study underscores the pivotal role of BESS in supporting renewable energy integration, offering insights crucial for global energy transition initiatives. Importantly, the study also evaluates the environmental impact of BESS deployment, including life cycle analysis and considerations for battery recycling.

articleTitle: Impact Analysis and Optimized Solution for Electric Vehicle Integration in Densely Populated Distribution Networks: A Case Study in Bangladesh
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: This study investigates the dynamics of electric vehicle (EV) integration within an authentic distribution network in Bangladesh by leveraging DigSilent Powerfactory for modeling. Through simulations encompassing 10%, 20%, and 30% EV integration in an 11 kV distributed system, the research scrutinizes the network's robustness against heightened loads from both EV charging stations and household EV charging. By employing load flow and quasi-dynamic simulations, the analysis accounts for the stochastic variability in load consumption, mirroring the load profile of Bangladesh based on peak/off-peak hours and seasonal fluctuations. Key parameters, including voltage profiles, active power flows, and power losses, are thoroughly examined to reveal the network's resilience to accommodate augmented loads. The outcomes advocate for optimization strategies for both residential and commercial charging stations, showcasing how the existing infrastructure can adeptly absorb additional charging facilities without requiring extensive network overhauls and hence improving the hosting capacity. This study offers pragmatic insights for distribution system operators in Bangladesh and beyond, providing a framework for managing challenges arising from the escalating integration of electric vehicles.

articleTitle: Profitability of Battolyser for Green Hydrogen Production in a Photovoltaic Farm: Techno-Economic Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: Recent trends in global energy strategies emphasize sustainability, where the integration of renewable energy sources and energy storage technologies becomes crucial. This integration is critical in ensuring grid reliability and reducing carbon footprints. This research contributes to the reduction of the reliance on conventional energy sources and facilitates the transition to a sustainable energy future. The findings will contribute to the optimization of smart electrical grids with integrated renewable energy sources, batteries, and innovative battolysers for green hydrogen production and storage. The smart grid architecture includes photovoltaic panels and energy storage systems, such as batteries. This off-grid energy system will serve to feed a remote community in energy. The inclusion of batteries serves as short-term energy storage to address temporal disparities between energy generation and demand. To respond to various off-grid conditions such as fluctuating renewable energy inputs and dynamic energy demand patterns, we propose adding a battolyzer to the smart grid. A battolyzer is a combined system to produce green hydrogen. It plays the double role of a battery and an electrolyzer. It stores electrical energy and when the battery is charged, the energy is used through the electrolysis to produce hydrogen. A techno-economic analysis is performed to justify the integration of the battolyzer in the smart grid to manage the electrical energy produced through photovoltaic panels and to enhance the grid's reliability. The study assesses the cost of energy with only electricity storage and then with electricity and hydrogen storage.

articleTitle: Optimal Demand Side Load Management for Smart House Based on User's Satisfaction
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: Over the past few decades, the conventional and one-way electricity grid has undergone a remarkable evolution towards a smart and two-ways grid system. With the demand-responsive capability of smart grids, residential customers can use their devices on demand to obtain economic benefits in return, and increasing their satisfaction. In this context, this paper proposes an on-demand side load management technique to optimally control home appliances, such that user satisfaction is maximized with lowest cost, and the peak-to- average ratio is minimal. The main contributions of this article are: the integration of user satisfaction concept in the planning of home appliances then the use of a multi-objective optimization algorithm instead of traditional single-objective optimization. The input data required by the algorithm includes device types, device power, device usage period, electricity cost, as well as user satisfaction related to each electrical device used every hour of the day. The effectiveness of the proposed technique is proven by comparison between four scenarios. The results revealed that the proposed optimization algorithm was the best solution to achieve maximum benefits in terms of energy cost, peak-to-average ratio and user satisfaction.

articleTitle: Analysis of Low-Cycle Lead Acid Battery Aging in Off-grid PV Systems with Changing Consumptions
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: It is crucial to balance energy production and consumption at all times, including the integration of renewable energy plants and electrical vehicles. In today's world, managing renewable energy production alone is not sufficient. To achieve more profit, it is important to consider the consumption of customers since consumption behaviors change at every second. An off-grid system using lead-acid batteries and photovoltaic panels has been developed in this study. After the design, the realized hourly consumption of Turkey in 2023 is scaled, so that a customer consumes an average power of 1,615 watts per hour whereas yearly consumption is 14,149.55 kWh. The Maltepe neighborhood in Izmir, Turkey has been selected for analysis. The study is created by distributing seven different consumption cases. These cases are divided into the following categories: only day, only night, only peak, day-night-peak, day-peak, day-night, and night-peak. The energy needs are met by photovoltaic solar panels with a power of 13.5 kWp and lead-acid batteries with a capacity of 2,324 Ah. Using the PVSyst solar software, production can be matched to hourly consumption in various scenarios. In only the night consumption case, the battery lifespan is 2.5 years, while in the day consumption case it lasts 4.6 years. According to the results, consuming energy during the daytime can extend the battery life in off-grid systems.

articleTitle: A Survey on Converter Types and Energy Sources Used in Fuel Cell Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: In this paper, DC/DC converter types and energy sources including Battery (B), Ultracapacitor (UC), Supercapacitor (SC), and Fuel Cell (FC) used in Fuel Cell Electric Vehicles (FCEVs) are searched. Two type DC/DC converters are examined. While type 1 converter has lower voltage gain, higher current ripple, the voltage gain of type 2 with a capacitor clamped and FC lifespan are high. Furthermore, voltage stresses on semiconductors of the type 2 are also lower than type 1. For this reason, type 2 converter can be chosen for the FCEVs. The other topic handled in this study is the energy sources. Some features which are high power and energy densities, long lifespan, low operating temperature ranges, fast charge and discharge are expected from the energy sources to be used in the FCEVs. While the UCs meet these properties compared to the Bs, the energy density of them is low and the production cost is high. This limits the use of it in the FCEVs. The SCs can store the energy per unit compared to the UCs. This provide an advantage for long-term energy storage applications. However, the operating temperature ranges of them are limited compared to the UCs. The FCs offer high energy density and continuous operation but some challenges related to fuel availability and complexity. The choice between the FC and SC depends on the specific requirements of the application, including power and energy demands, operating conditions, and cost considerations. According to road conditions especially on a negative sloping road, recovering the energy by the regenerative braking is quite hard in the FCEVs with only FC. Hence, a FC/SC hybrid system can be preferred for providing a higher power density than the batteries.

articleTitle: Performance Study of two PV Power Plants in Algeria
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: This paper aims to highlight the importance of the application of the IEC 61724 standard in the study of the performance analysis of photovoltaic power plants on a monthly and annual scale. Likewise, the comparison of two photovoltaic power plants with two different climates was carried out in order to determine the effect of climatic parameters on the analysis of photovoltaic performances. All data from the Saida and Adrar photovoltaic power plants for 2018 and the data from the Saida1 field for one month in 2019 were used. The results of the performance analysis according to the indicated standard show that the Saida PV power plant performs better than the Adrar PV power plant, which is due to the effect of increasing the ambient temperature. Increasing ambient temperature increases losses, decreases system efficiency and performance ratio. It presents a key element in the proper functioning of PV plants.

articleTitle: Optimizing DFIG-Based Wind Energy Systems Using Hybrid Control Combining MPC and PSO
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: This paper presents a wind energy system equipped with a double-fed induction generator (DFIG) controlled by a Model Predictive Control - Particle Swarm Optimization (MPC-PSO) controller. The integration of Model Predictive Control-Particle Swarm Optimization (MPC-PSO) combines the predictive accuracy of MPC with the global optimization abilities of PSO, making it proficient in managing the complexities and nonlinearities of DFIGs. The primary control objectives of the system are to optimize power output, regulate voltage, and maintain frequency stability. To achieve these goals, the following steps should be taken: (i) use Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) control to adjust the DFIG's rotor speed to enhance power extraction; (ii) precisely control the rotor-side and grid-side converter currents to reduce harmonics; (iii) stabilize the DC bus voltage; and (iv) manage reactive power via the grid-side converter to facilitate power factor correction (PFC) at the grid interface. The proposed controller is applied to loop current control in rotor-side and grid-side converters, demonstrating precise regulation and enhanced power quality. The MPC-PSO controller enhanced active power by 93.75 % and reactive power management by 48.52%, while also reducing Total Harmonic Distortion by 67.81 % for grid current. These results demonstrate a significant improvement in wind energy conversion system performance.

articleTitle: Optimization of Geothermal Energy Piles Design Parameters to Enhance Thermal Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: Energy piles, a type of geothermal heat exchanger integrated into building foundations, offer a sustainable solution for heating and cooling by utilizing the thermal properties of the ground. However, the design of energy piles involves complex interactions between thermal and mechanical behaviors. This paper addresses critical optimization issues, including pile geometry, ground heat exchanger tube configurations, concrete composition, and fluid dynamics. The study aims to enhance thermal efficiency by examining these design parameters and their impacts. Through a comprehensive review of recent parametric studies, the paper identifies critical factors influencing energy pile performance and provides insights and recommendations for improving their design and efficiency. The key findings highlight the crucial role of optimizing pile size, tube spacing, concrete thermal conductivity, and fluid properties in developing efficient and durable energy pile systems. Additionally, the proposed optimization approach is validated by reviewing recent simulations and experimental studies on energy piles, confirming the reliability of the recommendations.

articleTitle: Optimal Sizing and Operation Strategies for Isolated Microgrid Integrating Green Hydrogen
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: This study investigates the optimal sizing and operation scenarios for an island microgrid located in 6<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> of October, Egypt. The proposed microgrid integrates a combination of renewable and clean energy technologies, including photovoltaic (PV) panels, battery energy storage system (BESS), and a green hydrogen energy storage system (GHESS). The microgrid will also house a cable factory, adding an additional load profile to consider. Homer Pro software is employed to model and optimize the microgrid design. To achieve this goal, the various operation scenarios across different days throughout the year are simulated using Homer Pro. These simulated scenarios considered the fluctuating availability of solar energy from the PV system, along with the varying energy demands of the factory load. For each scenario, Homer Pro is intelligently selects the most cost-effective combination of energy sources to meet the demand. This might involve using the PV system during peak sunlight hours, the BESS during periods of high demand or low solar production, and the GHESS with its Electrolyser and fuel cell for extended periods of low solar availability. The green hydrogen system utilize an Electrolyser, powered by excess renewable energy from the PV system, to split water into hydrogen and oxygen where the hydrogen is stored in the GHESS. When renewable energy is insufficient, a fuel cell is employed to convert the stored hydrogen back into electricity, powering the microgrid and the factory. The results provide valuable insights into the feasibility and optimal design of an island microgrid utilizing green hydrogen for enhanced energy security and sustainability in the isolated microgrid.

articleTitle: Energy Storage and Carbon Capture Peaker Plant Planning in Transitioning to Renewable Energies Against Weather Susceptibility
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: Renewable energies have emerged as leading so-lutions to combat greenhouse gas emissions. However, their inherent vulnerability to weather conditions hampers the pace of transition and raises concerns about the reliability of electric supply. Energy storage systems and peaker plants with natural gas generation can offset the limitations of renewable energies. But they are expensive and complex to plan due to the dynamic nature of renewable energy generation. This research presents a behavior model and a simulation method to optimize the capacities of such energy components. The simulation method can process hourly electricity data from 81 US regions nationwide. It aims to minimize the total annual generation cost while adhering to the target carbon dioxide generation by optimizing capacity allocations for renewable energies, energy storage systems, and carbon capture and storage. The proposed method lays the foundation for a simulation framework to analyze and plan energy component capacities to phase in renewable energies to a zero-emission power grid.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Renewable Energy Solutions: Induction Switched Reluctance Machine vs. Conventional Induction Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: The Induction Switched Reluctance Machine (ISRM) represents a groundbreaking advancement in electrical machine technology, showcasing exceptional torque and power density attributes. Its innovation lies in optimizing the flux path within the machine, achieved through strategically positioned short-circuit windings on the rotor. This design enables the ISRM to achieve remarkable electromechanical energy conversion efficiency, boasting superior torque density compared to conventional electrical machines. Notable features include a shortened flux path and minimal core loss, highlighting its exceptional performance metrics. While the ISRM demonstrates versatility across various domains, its significance shines particularly bright in the field of wind power turbines. Here, its ability to deliver high torque in demanding conditions is paramount. Our study focuses on evaluating a 12/10 ISRM through finite element simulations, with a specific emphasis on its suitability for wind turbine applications. By conducting a comparative analysis against an Induction Machine, a benchmark in the industry, we demonstrate the ISRM's superior performance in terms of torque output and efficiency.

articleTitle: Economic Study of Building Integrated Photovoltaics (BIPV) System in Scotland
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: Solar electricity is the most abundant and pure of all existing energy supplies, and one of the greatest methods to tap into this resource is building integrated photovoltaics (BIPV). This study emphasises the economic evaluation of the BIPV system to mitigate the misunderstanding of solar developers and customers about the cost-effectiveness of choosing the BIPV system. Therefore, there is a need to review the actual economic values of the current BIPV project to clarify the common misunderstanding of the high cost of the BIPV system. This 1 kWp grid-connected solar PV system has been designed using PVSYST software, and four different locations in Scotland have been chosen to study the significance of how location parameters affect a PV system's economic viability. Levelised cost of energy and payback periods are estimated to identify the financial benefits of the BIPV system. Moreover, the system design and calculations were done using different orientations of PV panels. The values that are obtained are plotted as 3D graphs using MATLAB software. The economic assessment revealed that the project is economically feasible at various combinations of façade orientation. Finally, the paper presents a conclusion and a set of recommendations. BIPVs are unique designs with diverse economic performances. The study confirms that understanding the country's financial parameters. The BIPV system is the best choice for architects looking to satisfy their customers looking to develop an economically viable, environmentally friendly, green, electricity-producing building.

articleTitle: Towards Better Energy Efficiency Through Coil-Based Electricity Consumption Forecasting in Steel Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: Forecasting electricity consumption with the possibly-highest accuracy is crucial for cost optimization, operational efficiency, competitiveness, contract negotiation, and achieving the global goals of sustainable development in steel manufacturing. This study focuses on identifying the most appropriate prediction algorithm for coil-based electricity consumption and the most effective implementation purposes in a steel company. Random Forest, Gradient-Boosted Trees, and Deep Neural Networks are preferred because they are suitable for the given problem and widely used for forecasting. The performance of the prediction models is evaluated based on the root mean squared error (RMSE) and the coefficient of determination (R-squared). Experiments show that the Random Forest model outperforms the Gradient-Boosted Trees and Deep Neural Network models. The results will provide benefits for many different purposes. Firstly, during contract negotiations, it will enable us to gain a competitive advantage when purchasing electricity in the day-ahead market. Secondly, in the production scheduling phase, the ones with the highest electricity consumption will be produced during the hours when there is the least demand at the most affordable prices. Finally, when prioritizing sales orders, the use of the existing capacity for orders with lower energy intensity or a higher profit margin will be ensured.

articleTitle: Electric Bus Public Transport Cybersecurity
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: The electric buses have been widely deployed in the recent years. Electrified public transport fleets may reach massive charging powers and electricity generation mix related carbon emissions, and electricity costs could be very high due to dynamic pricing tariffs. Charging coordination approaches gain importance to minimize the related electricity costs and carbon emissions, managing the charging durations based on the available parking times during the day. Such coordination systems can also be a potential target for cyberattacks, aiming to cause financial losses or interrupt public services. In this study, cybersecurity of public transport is taken into consideration analyzing cyberattack impacts. A real route, of Istanbul Municipality public transport is selected, and the related time schedules are considered. The study also takes into account the impact of rush hours (number of passengers per trip, changing energy consumption per km), traffic congestion (affecting trip times) and assigns busses to each trip, ensuring public transport service with no interruptions, considering the minimum time windows needed for charging the buses and satisfying the public transport mobility need of the community. The study proposes an algorithm for reducing costs in dynamic pricing tariffs, where the hourly pricing rate of electricity changes, or reducing carbon emission by performing low-carbon charging based on the carbon emission of the grid electricity generation mix. The proposed algorithm is compared with a deterministic charging methodology in which the buses are charged between each trip for a fixed duration. The impacts of a data swapping attack that targets the public transport fleet charging coordination system is investigated in simulations. The results are compared in terms of daily total electricity costs and carbon emissions of the whole fleet. All the data regarding gathered from the official resources to investigate realistic scenarios.

articleTitle: Improving Norwegian Power Transmission Flexibility Using a New Matheuristic Optimization Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: There is an increasing demand for transmission system operators to expand their participation in the electricity reserve markets, encompassing smaller businesses and house-holds that are currently excluded due to market constraints. These smaller entities require an aggregator's assistance to pool the loads of several minor actors, enabling their participation in the markets through an aggregator that can optimize bids. This paper introduces a matheuristic framework aimed at maximizing revenue in the Norwegian power reserve markets, showcasing the potential effectiveness of aggregators. The framework is utilized to analyze the optimal bidding strategies for an aggregator within the Norwegian Reserve Markets over two distinct time periods, using real market prices, flexible power capacity, and customer consumption data. The heuristics are evaluated and the outcomes are compared with those of a mathematical model. The matheuristic models achieved results ranging from 88–94 % relative to the corresponding mathematical model.

publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: 2024 5th International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering was successfully held in Izmir, Turkey from August 24-26, 2024. CGEE conference is an annual event. This annual event has been conducted since 2020. The conference aims to bring together researchers, practitioners, and professionals from the industry, academia, and government to discuss the latest research and development, as well as professional practices in the field of clean and green energy engineering.
